data.description: The asset data depend on the type of the asset. Asset data are available at runtime.

file.description: Properties related to the file of the asset.

variants.description: Properties for the different variants of the asset file.

dxt.description: Properties for the DXT variant of the asset file

etc1.description: Properties for the ETC1 variant of the asset file

etc2.description: Properties for the ETC2 variant of the asset file

pvr.description: Properties for the PVR variant of the asset file

basis.description: Properties for the BASIS variant of the asset file

i18n.description: A dictionary that holds localized versions of the asset file. Each key in the dictionary is the locale and each value is the asset `id`.

meta.description: Asset properties that depend on the type of the asset. Meta properties are available in the PlayCanvas Editor but not at runtime.

path.description: An array of folder asset `id`'s that represent the full path of the asset, if the asset is under one or more folders.

preload.description: If true the asset will be loaded during the preload phase of application set up.

exclude.description: Exclude asset from the project. If true, the asset will not be available at runtime and not be included in published builds.

source.description: Whether this is a source asset. A source asset is not included at runtime (e.g. FBX) but may have target assets that are generated from it (e.g. model assets).

source_asset_id.description: The `id` of the source asset that generated this asset.

type.description: The type of the asset. Can be: animation, animstategraph, audio, bundle, binary, container, cubemap, css, font, folder, json, html, gsplat, material, model, render, scene, script, shader, sprite, template, text, texture, textureatlas, wasm.

physics.description: Physics related settings for the scene.

gravity.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the gravity force.

fog.description: The type of fog used in the scene. Can be one of `pc.FOG_NONE`, `pc.FOG_LINEAR`, `pc.FOG_EXP`, `pc.FOG_EXP2`.

fog_start.description: The distance from the viewpoint where linear fog begins. This property is only valid if the fog property is set to `pc.FOG_LINEAR`.

fog_end.description: The distance from the viewpoint where linear fog reaches its maximum. This property is only valid if the fog property is set to `pc.FOG_LINEAR`.

fog_density.description: The density of the fog. This property is only valid if the fog property is set to `pc.FOG_EXP` or `pc.FOG_EXP2`.

fog_color.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the color of the fog.

global_ambient.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the color of the scene's ambient light.

gamma_correction.description: The gamma correction to apply when rendering the scene. Can be one of `pc.GAMMA_NONE`, `pc.GAMMA_SRGB`.

lightmapMode.description: The lightmap baking mode. Can be one of `pc.BAKE_COLOR`, `pc.BAKE_COLORDIR`.

tonemapping.description: The tonemapping transform to apply when writing fragments to the frame buffer. Can be: `pc.TONEMAP_NONE`, `pc.TONEMAP_LINEAR`, `pc.TONEMAP_FILMIC`, `pc.TONEMAP_HEJL`, `pc.TONEMAP_ACES`, `pc.TONEMAP_ACES2`, `pc.TONEMAP_NEUTRAL`.

exposure.description: The exposure value tweaks the overall brightness of the scene.

skybox.description: The `id` of the cubemap texture to be used as the scene's skybox.

skyMeshPosition.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the position of the sky mesh.

skyMeshRotation.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the rotation of the sky mesh.

skyMeshScale.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the scale of the sky mesh.

skyCenter.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the center of the sky mesh.

skyboxMip.description: The mip level of the skybox to be displayed. Only valid for prefiltered cubemap skyboxes.

skyDepthWrite.description: Whether the sky writes to the depth buffer.

skyboxRotation.description: An array of 3 numbers representing the rotation of the skybox.

lightmapFilterRange.description: A range parameter of the bilateral filter.

lightmapFilterSmoothness.description: A spatial parameter of the bilateral filter.

ambientBake.description: Enable baking the ambient lighting into lightmaps.

ambientBakeNumSamples.description: Number of samples to use when baking ambient.

ambientBakeSpherePart.description: How much of the sphere to include when baking ambient.

ambientBakeOcclusionBrightness.description: Specifies the ambient occlusion brightness. Typical range is -1 to 1.

ambientBakeOcclusionContrast.description: Specifies the ambient occlusion contrast. Typical range is -1 to 1.

lightingCells.description: Number of cells along each world-space axis the space containing lights is subdivided into.

lightingMaxLightsPerCell.description: Maximum number of lights a cell can store.

lightingMaxLights.description: Maximum number of lights the renderer supports. No upper bound is enforced.

lightingCookieAtlasResolution.description: Resolution of the atlas texture storing all non-directional cookie textures.

lightingShadowAtlasResolution.description: Resolution of the atlas texture storing all non-directional shadow textures.

lightingShadowType.description: The type of shadow filtering used by all shadows. Can be SHADOW_PCF1, SHADOW_PCF3 or SHADOW_PCF5.

gsplatRadialSorting.description: Sort gsplats by radial distance from the camera rather than along the view direction.

gsplatLodUpdateDistance.description: Camera travel distance (world units) that triggers a gsplat LOD update.

gsplatLodUpdateAngle.description: Camera rotation angle (degrees) that triggers a gsplat LOD update. 0 disables rotation-based updates, which also stop when gsplatLodBehindPenalty is 1.

gsplatLodBehindPenalty.description: Distance multiplier applied to gsplat nodes behind the camera when selecting LOD and ordering streamed loads. 1 means no penalty.

gsplatLodUnderfillLimit.description: Maximum number of LOD levels below optimal that may be used while the optimal data loads. 0 always waits for the optimal LOD.

gsplatSplatBudget.description: Number of splats rendered across all gsplats in the scene, used as set by gsplatSplatBudgetMode. 0 means no budget.

gsplatSplatBudgetMode.description: How gsplatSplatBudget is used. Can be: target (detail is raised until the budget is used), limit (the LOD distances of each gsplat decide the detail and the budget only lowers it to fit).

gsplatAlphaClip.description: Alpha threshold for the shadow, pick and prepass gsplat rendering.

gsplatAlphaClipForward.description: Alpha threshold below which splats are culled in the forward pass.

gsplatMinPixelSize.description: Minimum screen-space pixel size below which splats are discarded.

gsplatMinContribution.description: Minimum visual contribution below which splats are culled. 0 disables contribution culling.

gsplatFoveationStrength.description: Strength of foveated contribution culling towards the screen edges. 0 disables it.

gsplatFoveationCenter.description: Protected centre radius (NDC) within which foveation has no effect.

gsplatAntiAlias.description: Enable anti-aliasing compensation for splats trained with anti-aliasing.

gsplatUseFog.description: Whether gsplats are affected by scene fog.

gsplatColorUpdateAngle.description: Viewing-angle change (degrees) that triggers a gsplat spherical-harmonics color update. 0 updates every frame the camera moves.

gsplatCooldownTicks.description: Number of update ticks an unused streamed gsplat resource waits before unloading. 0 unloads immediately.

gsplatDataFormat.description: Work-buffer data format for gsplat rendering. Can be: compact, large.

gsplatEnableIds.description: Store a unique per-component id in the gsplat work buffer.

gsplatLodMode.description: Metric used to select gsplat LOD within the splat budget. Can be: error, distance. Deprecated in engine 2.23, ignored: LOD is always distance-based.

gsplatUseTonemap.description: Whether gsplats are affected by the camera's tone mapping and scene exposure.

resource_id.description: The unique GUID of the entity.

parent.description: The `resource_id` of the parent entity (null for the scene root).

children.description: An array that contains the `resource_id`'s of the entity's children.

position.description: The position of the entity in local space (x, y, z).

rotation.description: The rotation of the entity in local space (rx, ry, rz euler angles in degrees)

scale.description: The scale of the entity in local space (sx, sy, sz).

template_id.description: The `id` of the Template asset that this entity is linked to.

template_ent_ids.description: A dictionary of <`resource_id`, `resource_id`> pairs that maps the entity (and its children) to the respective Entities in the template asset.

components.description: A dictionary that contains the components of the entity and their data.

audiolistener.description: The data for the audiolistener component.

animation.description: The data for the (legacy) animation component.

speed.description: A multiplier for animation playback speed. 0 will freeze animation playback, and 1 represents the normal playback speed of the asset.

loop.description: If true, the animation will continue to loop back to the start on completion. Otherwise, the animation will come to a stop on its final frame.

activate.description: If true, the component will start playing the animation on load.

anim.description: The data for the anim component.

animationAssets.description: A dictionary that holds the animation assets used by this component. Each key is a string which represents a path to a particular state in the graph e.g. "LocomotionLayer:Walking".

asset.description: The `id` of the The animation asset.

speed.description: A multiplier for animation playback speed. 0 will freeze animation playback, and 1 represents the normal playback speed.

activate.description: If true, the component will start playing the anim state graph on load.

rootBone.description: The `resource_id` of the entity that this anim component should use as the root of the animation hierarchy.

normalizeWeights.description: If true, the weights of all layers will be normalized together. Otherwise, the animations of each layer will be applied independently.

masks.description: The layer masks associated with this component.

mask.description: A set of paths to bones in the current model that should be animated by the layer.

value.description: Whether this bone should also be included in the mask.

children.description: Whether the children of this bone should also be included in the mask.

sound.description: The data for the sound component.

volume.description: The volume modifier to play the audio with. The volume of each slot is multiplied with this value.

pitch.description: The pitch to playback the audio at. A value of 1 means the audio is played back at the original pitch. The pitch of each slot is multiplied with this value.

positional.description: If true, the component will play back audio assets as if played from the location of the entity in 3D space.

refDistance.description: The reference distance for reducing volume as the sound source moves further from the listener.

maxDistance.description: The maximum distance from the listener at which audio falloff stops. Note the volume of the audio is not 0 after this distance, but just doesn't fall off anymore.

rollOffFactor.description: The rate at which volume fall-off occurs.

distanceModel.description: Determines which algorithm to use to reduce the volume of the audio as it moves away from the listener. Can be one of: "inverse", "linear", "exponential".

slots.description: A dictionary of sound slots. Each sound slot controls playback of an audio asset. Each key in the dictionary is a number representing the index of each sound slot.

name.description: The name of the sound slot

volume.description: The volume modifier to play the audio with.

pitch.description: The pitch to playback the audio at. A value of 1 means the audio is played back at the original pitch.

asset.description: The `id` of the audio asset that can be played from this sound slot.

startTime.description: The start time from which the sound will start playing.

duration.description: The duration of the sound that the slot will play starting from startTime.

loop.description: If true, the slot will loop playback continuously. Otherwise, it will be played once to completion.

autoPlay.description: If true, the slot will be played on load. Otherwise, sound slots will need to be played by scripts.

overlap.description: If true then sounds played from slot will be played independently of each other. Otherwise the slot will first stop the current sound before starting the new one.

camera.description: The data for the camera component.

clearColorBuffer.description: If true, the camera will explicitly clear its render target to the chosen clear color before rendering the scene.

clearColor.description: The color used to clear the camera's render target.

clearDepthBuffer.description: If true, the camera will explicitly clear the depth buffer of its render target before rendering the scene.

projection.description: The projection type of the camera. Can be `pc.PROJECTION_PERSPECTIVE` or `pc.PROJECTION_ORTHOGRAPHIC`.

fov.description: The angle (in degrees) between top and bottom clip planes of a perspective camera.

frustumCulling.description: Controls the culling of mesh instances against the camera frustum. If true, culling is enabled. If false, all mesh instances in the scene are rendered by the camera, regardless of visibility.

orthoHeight.description: The distance in world units between the top and bottom clip planes of an orthographic camera.

nearClip.description: The distance in camera space from the camera's eye point to the near plane.

farClip.description: The distance in camera space from the camera's eye point to the far plane.

priority.description: A number that defines the order in which camera views are rendered by the engine. Smaller numbers are rendered first.

rect.description: An array of 4 numbers that represents the rectangle that specifies the viewport onto the camera's attached render target. This allows you to implement features like split-screen or picture-in-picture. It is defined by normalised coordinates (0 to 1) in the following format: [The lower left x coordinate, The lower left y coordinate, The width of the rectangle, The height of the rectangle].

layers.description: An array of layer id's that this camera will render.

toneMapping.description: The tonemapping transform to apply to the final color of the camera. Can be: `pc.TONEMAP_NONE`, `pc.TONEMAP_LINEAR`, `pc.TONEMAP_FILMIC`, `pc.TONEMAP_HEJL`, `pc.TONEMAP_ACES`, `pc.TONEMAP_ACES2`, `pc.TONEMAP_NEUTRAL, `pc.TONEMAP_AGX`, `pc.TONEMAP_AGX_PUNCHY`.

gammaCorrection.description: The gamma correction to apply to the final color of the camera. Can be: `pc.GAMMA_NONE`, `pc.GAMMA_SRGB`.

collision.description: The data for the collision component.

type.description: The type of collision primitive. Can be: box, sphere, capsulse, cylinder, mesh.

halfExtents.description: The half-extents of the collision box. This is an array of 3 numbers: local space half-width, half-height, and half-depth.

radius.description: The radius of the capsule/cylinder body.

axis.description: Aligns the capsule/cylinder with the local-space X, Y or Z axis of the entity

height.description: The tip-to-tip height of the capsule/cylinder.

convexHull.description: If true, the collision shape will be a convex hull.

asset.description: The `id` of the model asset that will be used as a source for the triangle-based collision mesh.

renderAsset.description: The `id` of the render asset that will be used as a source for the triangle-based collision mesh.

linearOffset.description: The positional offset of the collision shape from the Entity position along the local axes.

angularOffset.description: The rotational offset of the collision shape from the Entity rotation in local space.

rigidbody.description: The data for the rigidbody component.

type.description: The type of RigidBody determines how it is simulated. Can be one of: static, dynamic, kinematic.

linearDamping.description: Controls the rate at which a body loses linear velocity over time.

angularDamping.description: Controls the rate at which a body loses angular velocity over time.

linearFactor.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the scaling factor for linear movement of the body in each axis.

angularFactor.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the scaling factor for angular movement of the body in each axis.

friction.description: The friction value used when contacts occur between two bodies.

restitution.description: The amount of energy lost when two objects collide, this determines the bounciness of the object.

rollingFriction.description: The rolling friction applied to the body. Prevents round objects from rolling indefinitely.

gravityScale.description: Scale applied to the world gravity for this body. Dynamic bodies only.

light.description: The data for the light component.

type.description: The type of light. Can be: directional, spot, omni.

bake.description: If true the light will be rendered into lightmaps.

bakeArea.description: If bake is enabled, specifies the directional light penumbra angle in degrees, allowing soft shadows. Defaults to 0.

bakeNumSamples.description: If bake is enabled, specifies the number of samples used to bake this light into the lightmap.

bakeDir.description: If true and `bake` is true, the light's direction will contribute to directional lightmaps.

affectDynamic.description: If true the light will affect non-lightmapped objects.

affectLightmapped.description: If true the light will affect lightmapped objects.

affectSpecularity.description: If true the light will affect material specularity. For directional light only. Defaults to true.

color.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the color of the emitted light.

intensity.description: The intensity of the light, this acts as a scalar value for the light's color. This value can exceed 1.

castShadows.description: If true, the light will cause shadow casting models to cast shadows.

shadowUpdateMode.description: Tells the renderer how often shadows must be updated for this light. Options:`pc.SHADOWUPDATE_NONE`: Don't render shadows. `pc.SHADOWUPDATE_THISFRAME`: Render shadows only once (then automatically switches to `pc.SHADOWUPDATE_NONE`). `pc.SHADOWUPDATE_REALTIME`: Render shadows every frame (default).

shadowType.description: Type of shadows being rendered by this light. Options: `pc.SHADOW_PCF3`: Render packed depth, can be used for PCF sampling. `pc.SHADOW_PCF5`: Render depth buffer only, can be used for better hardware-accelerated PCF sampling. Requires WebGL2. Falls back to `pc.SHADOW_PCF3` on WebGL 1.0. `pc.SHADOW_VSM8`: Render packed variance shadow map. All shadow receivers must also cast shadows for this mode to work correctly. `pc.SHADOW_VSM16`: Render 16-bit exponential variance shadow map. Requires OES_texture_half_float extension. Falls back to `pc.SHADOW_VSM8`, if not supported. `pc.SHADOW_VSM32`: Render 32-bit exponential variance shadow map. Requires OES_texture_float extension. Falls back to `pc.SHADOW_VSM16`, if not supported.

vsmBlurMode.description: Blurring mode for variance shadow maps: `pc.BLUR_BOX`: Box filter. `pc.BLUR_GAUSSIAN`: Gaussian filter. May look smoother than box, but requires more samples.

vsmBlurSize.description: Number of samples used for blurring a variance shadow map. Only uneven numbers work, even are incremented. Minimum value is 1, maximum is 25

vsmBias.description: Constant depth offset applied to a shadow map that enables the tuning of shadows in order to eliminate rendering artifacts, namely 'shadow acne' and 'peter-panning'

shadowDistance.description: The shadow distance is the maximum distance from the camera beyond which shadows that come from Directional Lights are no longer visible. Smaller values produce more detailed shadows. The closer the limit the less shadow data has to be mapped to, and represented by, any shadow map; shadow map pixels are mapped spatially and so the less distance the shadow map has to cover, the smaller the pixels and so the more resolution any shadow has.

shadowIntensity.description: The intensity of the shadow darkening, 1 being shadows are entirely black.

shadowResolution.description: The size of the texture used for the shadow map.

cascadeDistribution.description: The distribution of subdivision of the camera frustum for individual shadow cascades.

shadowBias.description: Constant depth offset applied to a shadow map that enables the tuning of shadows in order to eliminate rendering artifacts, namely 'shadow acne' and 'peter-panning'.

penumbraSize.description: Size of the penumbra for PCSS (Percentage Closer Soft Shadows). A larger value produces softer shadow edges.

penumbraFalloff.description: Falloff rate for shadow penumbra for PCSS. Controls how quickly the shadow edge transitions from hard to soft.

range.description: The distance from the spotlight source at which its contribution falls to zero.

falloffMode.description: Controls the rate at which a light attentuates from its position.

innerConeAngle.description: The angle at which the spotlight cone starts to fade off. The angle is specified in degrees. Affects spot lights only.

outerConeAngle.description: The angle at which the spotlight cone has faded to nothing. The angle is specified in degrees. Affects spot lights only.

shape.description: The shape of the light source. Can be: `pc.LIGHTSHAPE_PUNCTUAL`, `pc.LIGHTSHAPE_RECT`, `pc.LIGHTSHAPE_DISK`, `pc.LIGHTSHAPE_SPHERE`.

cookieAsset.description: The id of a texture asset that represents that light cookie.

cookie.description: The id of a projection texture asset. Must be 2D for spot and cubemap for omni (ignored if incorrect type is used).

cookieFalloff.description: Toggle normal spotlight falloff when projection texture is used. When set to false, spotlight will work like a pure texture projector (only fading with distance).

cookieChannel.description: Color channels of the projection texture to use. Can be "r", "g", "b", "a", "rgb" or any swizzled combination.

layers.description: An array of layer id's that this light will affect.

model.description: The data for the (legacy) model component.

type.description: The type of the model to be rendered. Can be: asset, box, capsule, cone, cylinder, sphere.

asset.description: The `id` of the model asset rendered by this model component.

materialAsset.description: The `id` of the material asset that will be used to render the model (only applies to primitives).

castShadows.description: If true, the model rendered by this component will cast shadows onto other models in the scene.

castShadowsLightmap.description: If true, this model will cast shadows when rendering lightmaps.

receiveShadows.description: If true, the model rendered by this component will receive shadows cast by other models in the scene.

lightmapped.description: If true, this model will be lightmapped after using lightmapper.bake().

lightmapSizeMultiplier.description: Changing this value will affect resolution of lightmaps for this model.

mapping.description: A dictionary that maps a material asset to each mesh instance. Each key is the mesh instance index and each value is the asset `id`.

layers.description: An array of layer id's that this model belongs to. When a model belongs to multiple layers it will be rendered multiple times.

batchGroupId.description: The batch group id that this model belongs to. The engine will attempt to batch models in the same batch group to reduce draw calls.

aabbCenter.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the center of the AABB to be used.

aabbHalfExtents.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the half extents of the AABB to be used.

particlesystem.description: The data for the particlesystem component.

autoPlay.description: If true, the particle system will play immediately on creation. If false, you will need to call the particle system component's play function from script.

numParticles.description: The maximum number of particles managed by this particle system.

lifetime.description: The length of time in seconds between a particle's birth and its death.

rate.description: The bounds of the time range defining the interval in seconds between particle births. The time for the next particle emission will be chosen at random between `rate` and `rate2`.

rate2.description: The bounds of the time range defining the interval in seconds between particle births. The time for the next particle emission will be chosen at random between `rate` and `rate2`.

startAngle.description: The bounds of the initial particle rotation specified in degrees. For each particle, this angle is chosen at random between `startAngle` and `startAngle2`.

startAngle2.description: The bounds of the initial particle rotation specified in degrees. For each particle, this angle is chosen at random between `startAngle` and `startAngle2`.

loop.description: If true, the particle system will emit indefinitely. Otherwise, it will emit the number of particles specified by the `numParticles` property and then stop.

preWarm.description: If true, the particle system will be initialized as though it had already completed a full cycle. This option is only available for looping particle systems.

lighting.description: If true, the particle will be lit by the directional and ambient light in the scene. In some circumstances, it may be advisable to set a normal map on the particle system in order to achieve more realistic lighting.

useFog.description: If true, the particles are affected by scene fog.

useTonemap.description: If true, the particles are affected by the camera's tone mapping and scene exposure.

halfLambert.description: If true avoid particles looking too flat when lights appear to be shining towards the back sides of the particles. It is a completely non-physical lighting model but can give more pleasing visual results. This option is only available when `lighting` is enabled.

intensity.description: Scales the color of particles to allow them to have arbitrary brightness.

depthWrite.description: If true, the particles will write depth information to the depth buffer. If false, the depth buffer is left unchanged and particles will be guaranteed to overwrite one another in the order in which they are rendered.

depthSoftening.description: This variable value determines how much particles fade out as they get closer to another surface. This avoids the situation where particles appear to cut into surfaces.

sort.description: Sorting mode gives you control over the order in which particles are rendered. The options are: `pc.PARTICLESORT_NONE`: Particles are rendered in arbitrary order. When this option is selected, the particle system is simulated on the GPU (if the underlying hardware supports floating point textures) and it is recommended you use this setting to get the best performance. `pc.PARTICLESORT_DISTANCE`: Particles are sorted on the CPU and rendered in back to front order (in terms of camera z depth). `pc.PARTICLESORT_NEWER_FIRST`: Particles are sorted on the CPU and rendered in age order, youngest first. `pc.PARTICLESORT_OLDER_FIRST`: Particles are sorted on the CPU and rendered in age order, oldest first.

blendType.description: The blending mode determines how particles are composited when they are written to the frame buffer.

stretch.description: A value in world units that controls the amount by which particles are stretched based on their velocity. Particles are stretched from their center towards their previous position.

alignToMotion.description: If true orient particles in their direction of motion.

emitterShape.description: Shape of the emitter. Can be: `pc.EMITTERSHAPE_BOX`, `pc.EMITTERSHAPE_SPHERE`.

emitterExtents.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the half extents of a local space bounding box within which particles are spawned at random positions.

emitterExtentsInner.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the exception volume of a local space bounding box within which particles are not spawned.

orientation.description: Orientation mode controls particle planes facing. The options are: `pc.PARTICLEORIENTATION_SCREEN`: Particles are facing camera. `pc.PARTICLEORIENTATION_WORLD`: User defines world space normal to set planes orientation. `pc.PARTICLEORIENTATION_EMITTER`: Similar to previous, but the normal is affected by emitter(entity) transformation.

particleNormal.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents either world or emitter space vector to define particle plane orientation.

emitterRadius.description: The radius within which particles are spawned at random positions.

emitterRadiusInner.description: The inner sphere radius within which particles are not spawned

animTilesX.description: Number of horizontal tiles in the sprite sheet.

animTilesY.description: Number of vertical tiles in the sprite sheet.

animStartFrame.description: Sprite sheet frame in animation to begin animating from.

animNumFrames.description: Number of sprite sheet frames in each animation.

animNumAnimations.description: Number of animations contained in the sprite sheet.

animIndex.description: The animation from the sprite sheet to play for each particle in the system

randomizeAnimIndex.description: If true then each particle will play a randomly selected animation from the sprite sheet, otherwise it always use the animation specified by `animIndex`.

animSpeed.description: Sprite sheet animation speed. 1 = particle lifetime, 2 = twice during lifetime etc...

animLoop.description: If true then the sprite sheet animation will repeat indefinitely

wrapBounds.description: An array of 3 numbers that represents the world space AABB volume centered on the owner entity's position. If a particle crosses the boundary of one side of the volume, it teleports to the opposite side. You can use this to make environmental effects like rain by moving a wrapped emitter's owner entity.

colorMapAsset.description: The `id` of the color map texture asset to apply to all particles in the system. If no texture asset is assigned, a default spot texture is used.

normalMapAsset.description: The `id` of the normal map texture asset to apply to all particles in the system. Applying a normal map can make billboard particles appear more consistent with the scenes lighting.

mesh.description: The id of a model asset. The first mesh found in the model is used to represent all particles rather than a flat billboard.

renderAsset.description: The id of a render asset which can be used instead of the model asset to render a mesh-based particle.

localSpace.description: Binds particles to emitter node transformation.

screenSpace.description: Renders particles in 2D screen space. This needs to be set when particle system is part of hierarchy with screen component at its root, and allows particle system to integrate with the rendering of the element components.

localVelocityGraph.description: A curve defining how each particle's velocity with respect to the particle system's local coordinate system changes over time. If `localVelocityGraph2` is specified, local velocity will be a random lerp between both curves.

betweenCurves.description: If true then the system will randomize between `localVelocityGraph` and `localVelocityGraph2`.

keys.description: An array of 3 arrays. Each sub-array contains the keys for each curve in each axis.

items.description: The keys for this curve. Index 0 is the time and index 1 is the value. Index 2 is the next time, index 3 the next value and so on.

localVelocityGraph2.description: A curve defining how each particle's velocity with respect to the particle system's local coordinate system changes over time. If specified, local velocity will be a random lerp between both curves.

keys.description: An array of 3 arrays. Each sub-array contains the keys for each curve in each axis.

items.description: The keys for this curve. Index 0 is the time and index 1 is the value. Index 2 is the next time, index 3 the next value and so on.

velocityGraph.description: A curve defining how each particle's velocity with respect to the world coordinate system changes over time. If `velocityGraph2` is specified, velocity will be a random lerp between both curves.

betweenCurves.description: If true then the system will randomize between `velocityGraph` and `velocityGraph2`.

keys.description: An array of 3 arrays. Each sub-array contains the keys for each curve in each axis.

items.description: The keys for this curve. Index 0 is the time and index 1 is the value. Index 2 is the next time, index 3 the next value and so on.

velocityGraph2.description: A curve defining how each particle's velocity with respect to the world coordinate system changes over time. If specified, velocity will be a random lerp between both curves.

keys.description: An array of 3 arrays. Each sub-array contains the keys for each curve in each axis.

items.description: The keys for this curve. Index 0 is the time and index 1 is the value. Index 2 is the next time, index 3 the next value and so on.
